frontmatter.title: qDRIFT: randomized Hamiltonian evolution
frontmatter.description: Primitive Pauli circuits, exact rational term sampling and separately checked averaged channels.

children.value: qDRIFT replaces a prescribed product-formula ordering with randomly chosen term exponentials. Larger coefficients are selected more often. Averaging over newly drawn complete circuits approximates the desired dynamics even when one circuit is a poor approximation to the evolution operator

Executed evidence consists of bounded ideal circuit/channel checks and seeded classical sampling, with actual circuit exports and a reproduced companion notebook. The small study contains one readout from each freshly selected trajectory. Its outputs are a channel and a measured observable, rather than one deterministic coherent evolution oracle. Physical estimates and formalization remain planned.

children.value: The records distinguish the averaged channel, the empirical average of saved circuit channels and individual trajectory means. The plots show channel-error curves, individual trajectory expectations, the ideal mixture mean and the mean of one classically sampled full Z-readout per trajectory, scored by bit zero. These are ideal simulation results, not QPU measurements.
The reported spectral superoperator norm is the Hilbert–Schmidt-induced

children.html: 2→22\to22→2

children.value: norm. Normalized Choi trace distance, fixed-input trace distance and observable bias are separate diagnostics. None is a computed diamond norm. CP/TP follow analytically from a mixture of ideal unitary channels; floating-point Choi eigenvalue and trace checks are implementation diagnostics, not interval or formal certificates.

Repeating readout on one saved seed estimates that circuit’s expectation. Freshly drawing a complete schedule before each readout instead estimates the averaged-channel expectation. Those experiments have different joint distributions and must not share an unsupported confidence claim.

children.value: The 32-trial examples deliberately have broad confidence intervals. Their seeded realization does not empirically validate the analytic coverage statement. Hamiltonian channel bias, scalar gate rounding, synthesis error, statistical precision and physical failures have separate budgets. Controlled qDRIFT for phase estimation, grouped/importance-sampled variants and hardware-specific compilation remain planned.

No new physical estimate was executed. The next surface-code adapter must cost the complete measured workload, including resets, all draws’ circuit constructions, routing/idle exposure, readout and factories. Reset and feedforward assumptions must be explicit; an adapter that drops the initial resets does not cost the exported trial.

The scalar RZ conversion bound recorded in the ledger concerns binary64 angle conversion only. It excludes a concrete Clifford+T synthesis proof and Qiskit’s overall-phase accumulation/reduction for identity terms. Overall phase is immaterial to these measured channels, but exported QASM must not silently become a coherently controlled oracle. Any later physical comparison will preserve the frozen task, output, accuracy, success and hardware assumptions.
The circuit generator stops at 64 wires, 256 input terms, 512 exponentials and 100,000 primitive operations. Dense trajectory/channel references stop at three qubits
; an empirical study stops at 64 trajectories. A density matrix or unitary has

No Lean or Rocq proof is reproduced for qDRIFT here. The algebraic channel identity and numerical checks do not establish a compiler or physical fault-tolerance theorem.

Static pages and saved figures require no public kernel; live notebook controls use a local kernel or the configured Binder environment.
